source.ref: owner report and design asks 2026-09-23, on the live console

patch.detail:
OWNER REPORT 2026-09-23, looking at the live console: "The popup is still blinking but not as much. Re design this so there is better spacing and more vertical space for the calendar. The full calendar should always be in screen. Month scroll should be Up/Down. Put the Ask Vera in the bottom of the side bar."

THE BLINK AFTER THE BLINK. LIVE-472 fixed the big one (a ternary between two parents that remounted the whole calendar on every toggle). What was left is an ANIMATION, not a remount. `slide` is set at render time whenever the shown month changes and was never cleared, so the keyed month wrapper kept `motion-safe:animate-[calendarSlideNext_180ms_ease-out]` for the rest of the session. LIVE-472 physically MOVES that subtree between two DOM homes, and taking an element out of the document cancels its animations while putting it back starts them again from zero. So once the operator had paged a single month, every open and every close replayed the 180ms slide across the grid, underneath the dialog own 0.3s entrance: two animations over the same pixels on every toggle. That is exactly "smaller than before, still there". Proved by reading the live class list rather than by reasoning: mount, click Next, open, and the animate class is still on the node after the move. Fixed with one handler, `onAnimationEnd` clearing `slide`, so the class exists only while it is actually animating and a re-insertion has nothing to replay. Under reduced motion the class never applies, so no animationend fires and the flag stays set, which is inert.

WHY THE MONTH DID NOT FIT: THE CONSOLE PAID TWICE FOR THE SAME CHROME. Its own header carried the month, Today, Prev/Next and the view switcher, and then the grid rendered its OWN month title, its OWN Prev/Today/Next cluster and a SECOND view switcher, and Ask Vera took a full-width band above the panels. Four rows of furniture before a single date, and the month was cut off mid fourth week. The grid now takes `hostChrome`: inside the console it draws no month title, no jump panel, no paging cluster and no switcher, and the page grid is unchanged. The Loading live region stays either way, because a month still arriving has to be announced wherever the grid is mounted, and `focusMonthAnchor` falls back to the calendar root so LIVE-469 rule that focus never drops to the body still holds in a mount with no month button.

THE MONTH NOW FITS BECAUSE NOTHING BETWEEN THE OVERLAY AND THE CELLS IMPOSES A MINIMUM. The cell loses its `min-h-20 sm:min-h-28` floor (that floor is what pushed the last two weeks off the bottom), the day item column becomes a `min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-y-auto` scroller, and the six week rows divide whatever the stage row is: 117px per row at 1440x900, 196px at 1400 tall, about 62px on a 390x844 phone where the layout stacks. A busy day scrolls INSIDE its cell rather than the month growing, and under `fill` the cell renders every card instead of three plus a "+N more" that would have stranded the reader in a list view whose switcher is now gone. Off `fill` the three-item cap is unchanged and pinned.

ASK VERA IS THE SIDE BAR FOOTER. The agenda column became a flex column: the agenda scrolls, Vera is pinned under it behind its own hairline, capped so a long proposal scrolls rather than eating the column, and the footer is not rendered at all for a viewer who cannot edit rather than leaving an empty bordered strip. Vera travels as a SECOND portalled host, for the same reason LIVE-472 gives: writing it into two places is the bug this file exists to document.

UP AND DOWN PAGE THE MONTH, from the grid when it holds focus and from anywhere in the console, through the same switch as the existing keys and under the same typing and stacked-dialog guards. A new `verticalScrollTaker` walks up from the event target looking for something that can still scroll that way, so a busy day scrolling cell and the agenda keep their wheel and their arrows and only give them up when they have nowhere left to go. The shortcut sheet month row reads Up Down Left Right: no new row, no new string.

NOT FIXED, and worth its own row: the whole stage still remounts ONCE, right after hydration, because the portal host is gated on `isClient` so the server renders the panels inline and the second client render moves them. Proved with hydrateRoot and node identity. The two requirements are mutually exclusive as the code stands (React does not hydrate portal children, and the portal is load-bearing: React attaches listeners to the portal container). It costs no visible frame, since the deletion and insertion land in the same commit, but it costs the work and any state the grids had.2026-11-27 (SCAN-1344): the public Calendar tab stopped carrying its own team mode, per the owner ruling of 2026-11-25 ("Public only, link to team"). The team half of this row now lives on the team calendar at /spaces/<slug>/settings/calendar; the probe was rewritten to measure that.

2026-11-27 (SCAN-1344 follow-up): components/spaces/calendar-console.tsx was removed with the rest of the public tab's retired team mode; source re-pointed to the tab.
